Australia to Look Bigger on New World Map After Historic UN Vote

2026-09-13 Ben Graham (news.com.au) Australia, Equal Earth projection, UN, world map, Mercator, Greenland, cartography, Greg Lauer, OSGeo Oceania
Read the source article

Quick summary

Australia will appear roughly 10% larger relative to northern landmasses under the UN-endorsed Equal Earth projection, as geographer Greg Lauer explains how the shift changes visual perception of the continent's size compared to Greenland and Africa.

Key takeaways

  • The UN General Assembly voted 164-1 (US opposed) to endorse the Equal Earth projection over the Mercator map
  • Australia will appear about 10% larger relative to squeezed northern landmasses — not because Australia grows, but because Greenland shrinks
  • Geographer Greg Lauer: "The actual size doesn't change, but Greenland is a lot smaller and you can better see how Australia compares to Africa"
  • Africa is 14 times the size of Greenland, but the Mercator map makes them look similar
  • The Mercator map "was never wrong — it was right for navigation, but wrong for comparison"
  • Where the new map is centred matters: Australia/NZ prefer centring over the Pacific; UK-centred maps distort Australia and push NZ to the edge
  • Lauer: "Every flat map lies about something. The honest ones tell you what they're lying about"
  • The UN resolution is symbolic — no enforcement mechanism to replace classroom maps
